summary: Usage Forecast panel resets to zero during retention-tier migration causing false spike/dip alerts
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightChat reported that the "Usage Forecast" widget on their org dashboard shows a complete zeroed forecast for multiday windows intermittently during our retention-tier migration. This behavior caused their alerting rules (threshold-based anomaly alerts and scheduled spike/dip monitors) to produce automated notifications for a perceived traffic collapse and recovery.

Impact:
- Multiple automated P1/P2 alerts fired to the BrightChat on-call list and Slack channel (noise, interrupted SRE workflow).
- Dashboard snapshot exports (PDF/CSV) included zeroed forecast rows, affecting scheduled reports for executives.
- Potential business impact: teams acted on false alerts.

Environment:
- Customer org: BrightChat Inc. (enterprise)
- Console environment: prod, region us-east
- Affected pages: Organization > Dashboards > "Workspace Overview" (contains Usage Forecast panel)

Observed timing:
- First seen: 2026-03-10 09:12:33 UTC (customer screenshot attached)
- Recurrence: multiple windows between 2026-03-10 09:00 and 2026-03-10 17:00 during our retention migration job J-RET-2026-03-10

Expected behavior:
- Forecast panel should continue to show last-known forecast or degrade gracefully; it should not zero out historical forecasts during internal retention compaction/migration.

Actual behavior:
- Forecast panel metrics (20+ series) replaced with zeros for the selected date range and caused alert evaluations to treat the series as a drop to 0, triggering alerts.

Attachments:
- Customer screenshot (usage_forecast_zero_20260310.png) referenced in comment chain
- Console trace id: trace:org-7890:2026-03-10:09:12:33
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Ensure org has a Usage Forecast panel with daily forecast series and scheduled alerts.
2) Trigger retention-tier migration (internal test job that moves indices from hot->warm tier or run compaction).
3) While migration runs, open the Dashboard > Usage Forecast tile for a 7-day window and refresh.
4) Observe forecast time series replaced by zeros and scheduled alert evaluations run with zeroed input.

Note: Customer reproduction occurred during our 2026-03-10 retention compaction window.

investigation_notes:
- Repro steps in staging confirmed zero-fill behavior when forecast_aggregator received partial shard read errors from the storage layer (warm tier).
- Storage read path returned 504/timeout for warm shard migration windows; forecast_aggregator currently marks series as empty and zero-fills to maintain numeric types for charting.
- Temporal correlation: retention-migrator compaction tasks caused increased read latencies for indices being moved.
- Link to internal dashboard: https://console.redwood.test/internal/dashboards/retention-migrator-job-J-RET-2026-03-10 (internal)
- Suspected change: zero-fill policy introduced in commit 9a3d8f7 (forecast-agg: ensure numeric fallback).
resolution_notes:
Temporary mitigation applied 2026-03-12:
- Disabled noisy alert AL-4432 and AL-4433 for BrightChat (support action).
- Deployed a rollback in staging that changes forecast_aggregator fallback from zero-fill to 'use last-known non-null value' for up to 24 hours when shard reads fail (PR #2345).
- Scheduled a production-safe rollout with a feature flag to flip behavior during next maintenance window; engineering will monitor impact for 48 hours after rollout.

Planned permanent fix:
- Update forecast_aggregator to: 1) detect transient shard read timeouts and retry with backoff; 2) when partial data exists, merge available shard series instead of zero-filling; 3) expose an alert-suppression annotation for scheduled retention migrations.
